steps.content: Oak Casket listens to you quietly. Though you're talking about the spread of deadly Mania in the Drifter Camp, her expression is as serene as ever.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Don't worry. That Corpus probably won't come here.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Because it detests death, even more than ordinary humans.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Don't worry about me. If the situation becomes too bleak, I won't insist on staying either. I will take your advice and leave to find shelter.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Once this storm passes, I'll have to come back to bid farewell to many people. I must not miss such a grand ceremony.

<size=32>As Oak Casket says that, an eerie smile surfaces on her face, which makes Hella shiver again. You must admit that her job, her ability, where she works, and her... quirky humor, which she'd never revealed to you before, indeed make her quite scary.</size>
You hesitate for a moment and recall how she's helped you before. You decide to confess your request honestly.

steps.speaker: Options
options: I wish to borrow your vision to look for the Corpus.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You just said that its return has roused the long-dead Resonance from years ago. I take it that the people who died then were related to it as well?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I suppose so.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then could you please ask them what it really is, what kind of ability it has, why it comes here, and where it'll go?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If we don't find it and stop it, I'm afraid an even bigger disaster will be on its way.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It's one thing to listen to people's dying wishes, it's another to pry into private memories. Going deeper requires strong persistence. Since I don't have any, I can't fulfill your request.

steps.speaker: Options
options: Then can you take me there?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just now, when the shackles touched you, I could somehow feel the residual Mania you mentioned. If you allow me to use the shackles again and take me back there, I can look for the answer myself. I promise you I won't take away your freedom.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've tried my best. But I've run out of means to search for it relying on my own power. I need you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Tried your best... It's because of it you look so haggard now, am I right?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Before coming to me, did you touch any dangerous objects with the shackles? How many times? Are you sure you can take it?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: And now, you dare to take a peek at death?
Hecate grips your sleeve instinctively.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But this is the only way I can think of. I can't run away from the enemy, not when it's going to bring about a huge disaster.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've said that some noble ones redeemed my life with their own. They sacrificed themselves to stop the Black Rings. I can't let them down.
She stares into your eyes. After a long while, she speaks again.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Hmph... A hero who dares to face death head-on. You'll be praised.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Even if I turn you down, you'll find another risky way. Come on then...
She tugs off a glove and reaches out that hand to you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Due to its return, this spiritual field has been amplified as well. You should be able to hear something through the shackles, through me, now.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: If you've really made up your mind, then... I have something to tell you too.
Air is being squeezed out of your lungs. Your consciousness is gradually detached from your body. The woman in your sight begins to blur, and other figures crowd into your vision.
Shuffling figures and chaotic whispers travel through your consciousness and form a river, pushing you forward from the back.

Everything is blurry at first. Only messy emotions keep pouring in. Confusion, regret, attachment, bitterness. Unintelligible voices lurch inside you, making you turn around and go back up the stream.
Someone grabs your hand. The face is blurry but somehow familiar.
She nods.

steps.speaker: Gray Figure
steps.content: <color=#7683a2>Help me... Please...</color>
The vague phantom quivers and finally sighs softly, disappearing into the colorless stream, amid the suona melody coming from afar.
More turbulence keeps appearing. You find some familiar faces. Another person leaves this world. Sadness and depression gradually entangle your mind. You have no choice but to go on forward.
At last, at the delta in the center of the river, you see the familiar monument and the person waiting under it. Oak Casket stands there silently like she's listening to something.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This monument was built seven years ago to commemorate those <color=#fb9259>13,004 names</color>. I've been caressing their names, but I'm finally hearing their voices today.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I thought they might be related to the Corpus, but I didn't expect it to be that long ago. What happened then? What other secrets lie in the Drifter Camp's past?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I wasn't here at the time. I also only heard that story today.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Do you want to hear it too? Then... why don't you come closer?
She reaches out her hand to you again with a mysterious smile on her face.
The soft murmurs spread in your mind again. You hear... many warm voices.

steps.speaker: [White flash]
steps.content: [White flash]

steps.speaker: Chaotic Murmurs
steps.content: <color=#7683a2>No one is born a degenerate. We've only lost our soil... but... Hypercubes are found in contamination too. We're the ones who find them...</color>

steps.speaker: Chaotic Murmurs
steps.content: <color=#7683a2>Come at us. We're not even scared of those Syndican thugs... Let's go, go ahead... Show them what the West District should look like...</color>
You feel surrounded by many people. The cheerful, hopeful smiles push you forward, facing hope, dreams, and a vision for the future. You try to see clearly where they're going...
You see it. Ahead of you, somewhere shrouded by blurry mist, a red ring is slowly spinning.
It's a Black Ring.

steps.speaker: Chaotic Murmurs
steps.content: <color=#7683a2>Let's go. Go back to the Inner Bay. Go back to the mines. We'll reclaim our lives and dignity...</color>
No one hears you. As you hesitate, the figures pass through you. Only one person pauses to look back at you, as if attracted by something. You smell a familiar aroma.

steps.speaker: Hopeful Voice
steps.content: <color=#7683a2>Mom?</color>

steps.speaker: Hopeful Voice
steps.content: <color=#7683a2>Soon, I'll come back soon, wait for me...</color>
You remember. It smells like the delicious wraps by Lavina you tasted recently.

The procession passes straight through your outstretching arms. All the warmth, courage, and hope pour into that luminous ring, as if being sucked into a whirlpool in the sea, only to be torn, shattered, and sunk quietly.
You sense a familiar presence ahead. Mania, unique to that Corpus.

steps.speaker: (Scene change)
steps.content: [Scene Change]

You're back to the monument once again. Beside you is the flowing river of life and death. You don't feel pain, only crippling dejection. All the unredeemable broken emotions turn into tears you can't comprehend, falling down ceaselessly.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Aren't the emotions surrounding death too heavy for you? After all, you're very attached to the living world.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Do you want to continue?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's indeed here, in the memories of the deceased. Please let me continue. I'm so close to finding the answer.
As you speak, you reach out a hand to her eagerly. Oak Casket is silent for a moment, then lays her hand on your palm gently.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Is that so... Then... you must be careful...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The deceased who can leave their last words... are not all humans.

steps.speaker: [White flash]
steps.content: [White flash]
Your consciousness is trapped in darkness, prostrating in the mud. Your body feels heavy, like a million chaotic creatures are tangling behind you, dragging you backward.
A burning pain comes from your waist, but you can't feel anything from there on down. You hear yourself whimper.
It's... not over... yet...
Several people are chattering in front of you. You reach out your hand to crush their spirits, to extract their minds. Until death, they haven't become aware of your presence.
Don't want to die... I... don't want to die...

This body keeps going forward, keeps devouring every person it encounters along the way. You notice that this half-body is not trudging on alone. You turn around desperately, wanting to see what's dragging you.

A broken Black Ring floats somewhere even further away. In the center of the Black Ring, a huge dry corpse lies there, nailed into the filthy swamp by red luminous spikes. It's the other half of the body you've lost, long dead.

You wail, but no matter how much you devour, you can't make up for your frailty. Meanwhile, that supposedly dead half-body leaks out contamination like liquid fire, as if everything you devour ends up in its body.

<size=32>The burning pain of Mania contamination strikes you again. Your consciousness is being torn gradually, and somehow you begin to understand. This Mania is not naturally invisible. The contamination has been hidden, in the place where life meets death...</size>

steps.speaker: [White flash]
steps.content: [White flash]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Cough... Cough!!
Pain banishes you out of the illusory realm, back to the monument. You cough violently, feeling such sharp pain for the first time, as if you've really just experienced death.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It seems like you've gained a lot. Are you satisfied with your journey to death?
You're in so much pain, but you've genuinely gained something and found the answers to many questions.

steps.speaker: Options (Repeated Choice)
options: How did it conceal its Mania contamination?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <size=32>Seven years ago, or even earlier, there must have been a Black Ring eruption in the Inner Bay of the West District. That Black Ring plays a huge role in the Drifter Camp's history. I'm afraid those 13,004 people on the Romanesque monument are the ones sacrificed as ground zero.</size>

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: For some reason, that Black Ring was destroyed. The feeble Ring Master found its way to the Drifter Camp, perhaps instinctively tracing food that was similar to itself.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I just have to go and ask Julien, or Lavina, or the FAC. Someone must know about this. It can't stay hidden for long.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Its original body was chopped up and half of it was dead, left in that Black Ring. The other half has kept all its consciousness and is still on the loose.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <size=32>Perhaps due to the Ring Master's power, the two half-bodies, one dead and one alive, are still somehow deeply connected. The living half is out there spreading Mania and devouring humans' spiritual energy. The resulting contamination is transferred to the dead half.</size>

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's why no one can find it even after searching every corner of the camp... It's been accumulating power carefully until it can repair its own Black Ring.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Is this all true?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The deceased don't lie.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I must contact Nightingale and the FAC ASAP and start looking for that broken Black Ring now. It must have already accumulated a lot of power. If we don't stop it, the Black Ring will...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And the Drifter Camp too. We must evacuate everyone. If it can transfer contamination to the Inner Bay, it can transfer it here too. Since you've said... it detests death, that means...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It must want to get rid of its own memories of death!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We must hurry up. Oak Casket, please take me back!

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Go back? Back to here?
The water level rises and covers your ankles. Through the reflection in the water, you see Hella and Hecate, both looking at you worriedly.
...They seem agitated, which makes you anxious.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, wake up! A Black Ring has erupted, stop dozing! Wake up, please, I'm asking nicely! You...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ?! How come you're not breathing?
